previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman with type 1 diabetes, bilateral below-knee amputations, and a recent stump revision was admitted for fever, abdominal pain, and lethargy. She was found to have leukocytosis, acute kidney injury, and hyperkalemia. Initial concerns included pneumonia and possible C. difficile, but the source of infection was confirmed as a urinary tract infection caused by carbapenem-resistant ESBL Klebsiella. She was treated with intravenous meropenem and vancomycin, then transitioned to colistin after culture results. Her infection resolved, renal function normalized, and blood pressure stabilized with adjustment of metoprolol. She remained in the hospital for clinical observation until her father returned to assist at home, as she declined rehabilitation. She was discharged on home health for colistin administration, with stable vital signs and improving lab values.

Brief Hospital Course:
The patient was admitted primarily for her fevers and chills 
which likely showed an infectious cause. Otherwise the patient 
also had renal failure which was thought likely secondary to 
colistin use. These will be discussed by problems as detailed 
below.

#Bacteremia: The patient in the outpatient had a PICC line 
placed and was being treated for MDR e.coli and being treated 
with colistin. When she presented she was having fevers/chills 
despite already being on IV antibiotics. Blood cultures grew out 
coagulase negative staph species. Infectious disease consult was 
obtained who recommeneded that IV vancomycin be given for the 
staph species. They also recommeneded that the colistin be 
discontinued as she had ARF. Otherwise they recommeneded PO 
vancomycin for prophylactic treatment of C.Diff. Given that 
there was no growth of other organisms in the blood or the 
urine, the patient was started on vancomycin as the organism 
showed sensitivity to this antibiotic. The patient after the 
___ did not have any continued fevers and otherwise had 
negative blood cultures. She was discharged with 3 afebrile days 
as well as blood cultures which continue to be without any 
growth since ___. The patient on the day of discharge had a 
vancomycin level of 27.9, and elevated creatinine continuing to 
indicate decrased renal clearance. As a result given her 
previous renal function it was calculated that she would still 
have a therapeutic vancomycin level tomorrow on ___ which was 
the last day of vancomycin IV per infectious disease. Patient 
will continue on PO vancomycin for 7 days to prevent c.diff 
collitis.

# Acute renal failure: The patient presented in acute renal 
failure with an acutely elevated of creatinine to 4.3. The most 
likely culprit of the ARF is secondary to colistin which is 
known to be nephrotoxic. The patient had urine electrolytes 
drawn and FENa 7.7, FeUrea 77. Likely renal toxicity from 
colistin. The patient had a renal consult obtained who 
recommeneded discontinuation of the colistion as well as gentle 
hydration of the kidneys and blood sugar control. Otherwise all 
medications were renally dosed and gabapentin and ACE inhibitor 
were held. The patient had creatinine trended and was stabilized 
in the high 3s. Otherwise renal recommended that the patient be 
discharged and follow up with them in their clinic in early the 
following week and to have Dr. ___ her PCP draw labs 
including creatinine, BUNE, chem 10 and urine at follow up 
appointment after discharge.
 
# Hyperkalemia: This was felt likely secondary to acute renal 
failure. This resolved after checking electrolytes for a few 
days.
  
# T1DM: The patient had her insulin regimen from home restarted. 
This was not an active issue throughout this admission.
